clue.text: Started deep in wild part of Arizona

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the three preceding words run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Something kicked off far out in the untamed Arizona wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the thirteen letters of STARTED DEEP IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Painted Desert is a colourful badlands region in north-eastern Arizona.

clue.text: Student puts on a beard to appear as mediaeval scholar

indicators.note: the student is put on, wearing the beard, so the student's letter goes inside the two words

parts.note: the two words taken as written
L, the learner plate letter, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A pupil grows facial hair to look like a medieval academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts on' places L inside A BEARD, after ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a twelfth-century French philosopher and theologian, famed also for his love affair with Heloise.

clue.text: Lino definitely has a lump in it

indicators.note: this word says the answer sits inside the words it governs, as a run of their own consecutive letters
the phrase Lino definitely contains the letters running across its word break

explanation.surface: A linoleum floor covering certainly has a bump in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the join of 'liNO DEfinitely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot or swelling, such as a lymph node or a knob on a stem.

clue.text: Management team reduced by four, in effect

indicators.note: the management word is made smaller by having the roman numeral removed

parts.note: the executive is the body that runs a company
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: In practice, the board has lost four members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by' takes IV out of EXECUTIVE. 'effect' is the verb, to bring about; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect a plan is to carry it out or bring it about.

clue.text: Angle below pointer maybe revealing presence of marine creature

indicators.note: in a down entry, the angling word sits under the pointer word

parts.note: a pointer is a breed of gun dog, hence the 'maybe'
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Fishing beneath a pointing sign shows a sea creature is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags pointer as one example of a dog; 'revealing presence of' is link text.
explanation.definitionFit: The dogfish is a small shark of coastal waters.

clue.text: Only kind of music to listen to?

indicators.note: listening means the word for the music is heard rather than read

parts.note: soul is a genre of black American popular music

explanation.surface: Asks whether this is the one style of music worth hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUL and SOLE are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The sole survivor is the only survivor: both mean single, solitary.

clue.text: Deliver issue

definitions.meaning: to set free or let go
a record or film put out to the public

explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a captive is to free them, and a new issue of a record is a fresh launch onto the market.

clue.text: Girl in cutting down will show inconsistency

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed in the cutting-down word

parts.note: a contraction is a reduction or shortening
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl involved in a downsizing will expose a discrepancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting down' looks like part of the surface story of the girl, but it is the word for a reduction; 'will show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A contradiction is a statement or fact at odds with another, an inconsistency between them.

clue.text: Free to attend if you like?

parts.note: to go to something is to attend it
as you please means however you wish

explanation.surface: Asks whether one may turn up freely, if one wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-as-you-please describes something unrestricted, with no rules imposed.

clue.text: Extra fitting is late

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls; here, extra means over as in surplus
due means proper or appropriate

explanation.surface: An extra fitting has arrived behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by the expected time.

clue.text: Good, first-rate chap accepting trainee scientist

indicators.note: the first-rate and chap words take in the trainee's letter

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, read here with the digit 1 as letter I
L, the learner letter, stands for a trainee
Leo is a man's name

explanation.surface: A fine, top-class fellow takes on an apprentice researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, the classic mark of first-rate, is read with its digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist who championed the heliocentric view.

clue.text: Animal bit round filling

indicators.note: the round letter fills the small-amount word

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A creature nibbled around the edge of some filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' places O inside TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is a tailless amphibian resembling a frog.

clue.text: Approach number in state of collapse

indicators.note: the number letter goes in the collapse word

parts.note: ruin is a state of decay or collapse

explanation.surface: Contacting a figure while the system is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places N inside RUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is the final approach to something, such as a landing or finishing line.

clue.text: Body may provide service

definitions.meaning: a large amount or bulk of matter

explanation.surface: Says a corpse might be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a large body of matter, and Mass is the Catholic Eucharist service.

clue.text: Second charge causes panic

parts.note: a child in one's charge is in one's care

explanation.surface: A further accusation sends people into alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare is a sudden alarm or fright, such as a health panic.

clue.text: Soldier imprisoned in cooler is a villainous character

indicators.note: the soldier letters are locked inside the cooler word

parts.note: a fan cools the air
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier locked in the slammer is a bad lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like prison slang (it is that too); here it is a fan. 'is a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the criminal ringleader who trains pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist.

clue.text: French department's reached accidentally

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: an accident throws the letters of the word before it out of order

explanation.surface: A region of France has been reached by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accidentally' rearranges REACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardeche is a department in south-eastern France, named after its river.

clue.text: Firing instruction given at sea

definitions.meaning: dismissal from a job, as in getting the push
a sailors' call when hauling together on a rope

explanation.surface: An order shouted on board ship to open fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the heave-ho means sacking them, and the cry heave-ho kept sailors pulling in time.

clue.text: One with double money said to be unscrupulous

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: double asks for the money letter to be written twice over

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Someone with twice the cash is reckoned to be unprincipled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An immoral act breaks ethical standards, as an unscrupulous one does.

clue.text: Pain-relieving drug prescribed by doctor-take most of bottle

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
R is the prescription abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take

indicators.note: most of means the bottle word loses its last letter

parts.note: a phial is a small bottle for medicine

explanation.surface: A painkiller written up by a GP, who says drink most of the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the L of PHIAL to leave PHIA. 'prescribed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphia is an old name for morphine, the opiate painkiller.

clue.text: Guide on holiday is to get things moving

parts.note: to lead is to guide
someone off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: A tour guide on leave is the one to start activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin or open proceedings.

clue.text: Consider climber's route, say

indicators.note: say means the words for the climb are spoken and heard

parts.note: the way up is the route a climber takes

explanation.surface: Weigh up the line a mountaineer should take.
explanation.walkthrough: WAY UP and WEIGH UP sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh up options is to assess them carefully.

clue.text: Man is to leave before one in the morning

indicators.note: the leaving word comes first, ahead of the remaining pieces

parts.note: to will property is to leave it in a will
I is the Roman numeral one
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A fellow has to depart before 1 a.m.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'leave' looks like depart but means bequeath.
explanation.definitionFit: William is a man's given name.

clue.text: Cross-channel regular?

parts.note: a frequent visitor whose name for such a person crosses the Channel, being a French word adopted in English

explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a frequent visitor to a place, a term borrowed from French.

clue.text: Call time

definitions.meaning: a period, such as a school session

explanation.definitionFit: To term something is to call it by a name, and a term is a fixed period such as a school session.

clue.text: Main part is cut by a beam

indicators.note: the bulk word is split open by the single letter

parts.note: the bulk is the greater part

explanation.surface: Most of the structure is sliced through by a girder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by' puts A inside BULK; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A baulk is a roughly squared timber beam.

clue.text: French priest and American decline to return

indicators.note: returning means the decline word is read backwards

parts.note: to ebb is to decline

explanation.surface: A French cleric and a US citizen turn down going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns EBB, giving BBE; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbe is the French title for a clergyman.

clue.text: Sound of waterfall?

parts.note: not a cascade's roar but the noise made by something falling into water

explanation.definitionFit: A plop is the small sound of an object dropping into liquid.

clue.text: Stone work on Central Hall

indicators.note: in a down entry the work word sits on top of the following piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: central asks for the middle letters of the hall word

explanation.surface: Masonry work in the middle of a town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central' takes AL from the middle of HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: Tragedy dogging construction of hotel, see

indicators.note: dogging means following behind, so the see word trails the rest
construction means the hotel letters are built into a fresh order

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Disaster follows the building of a hotel, look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogging' means following at someone's heels, so LO comes last, after the rearranged hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy of the jealous Moor of Venice.

clue.text: I sulk, beset by problem over incentive

indicators.note: the sulk word is surrounded by the problem word
over means the problem word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a pet is a fit of sulking

explanation.surface: Someone sulks when hemmed in by trouble, needing motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in an across clue reverses the word, as if turned over; a pet as a sulk is the 'in a pet' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or stimulus behind an action.

clue.text: If I play Pam she spoils game

indicators.note: spoiling the preceding words wrecks their order into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cast as Pam in a show, a woman ruins the whole performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' rearranges IF I PLAY PAM SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy Families is a children's card game of collecting family sets.
